_comment: Copy for /issues and the six home cards. Each issue: title, punch (one angry line under the title), body, teaser (home card), image, face (alt text and placeholder caption), proofs [{text, href}]. Every proof links a source checked on 13 Oct 2026. tab_label and tab_order set the City / Country toggle; extra_from shows a site-wide figure under an issue when set.
title: Why put Labor last
lede: Six reasons we cannot miss this chance to vote Labor out.
help_line: If this is hitting hard: Lifeline 13 11 14 · Beyond Blue 1300 22 4636

groups.label: Devastating farmers
groups.sub: Towers, fines and foreign giants on your land

issues.title: Labor has devastated 180 years of generational Aussie farming
issues.punch: Families have farmed this land since 1834. Labor's ripping it up for towers.
issues.body: Labor took away your right to appeal renewable projects at VCAT, then gave its agency the power to fine you for blocking your own gate. VNI West has blown out from $3.6 billion to $7.6 billion, and AEMO warns it could hit $11.4 billion. Labor has even admitted one renewable energy zone was "no longer required" and scrapped it.
issues.teaser: Appeal rights gone, entry fines in, and VNI West costing double.
issues.face: An old bluestone homestead and shed with transmission towers marching across the wheat behind it
issues.caption: Generations of farming, cut through for a transmission line.

proofs.text: 14 March 2024: Labor removed third party appeals at VCAT for all new renewable projects.
Landholders who block VicGrid entry now face a penalty of up to $8,000.
AEMO: VNI West estimate more than doubled to $7.6 billion, and could reach $11.4 billion.
The Minister scrapped the central north renewable energy zone as "no longer required".

issues.title: Labor is sacrificing Aussie farms to foreign corporations
issues.punch: Aussie paddocks. Spanish and Canadian profits. Your power bill pays.
issues.body: VNI West is being developed by Spanish giant Iberdrola, lined up to build, own and operate it. The Western Renewables Link belongs to AusNet, owned by a consortium led by Canada's Brookfield, which told its own investors the line is a roughly $4 billion project with "potential returns". Farmers lose their land while foreign shareholders get their snouts in the trough.
issues.teaser: Spanish and Canadian giants own the lines. Snouts in the trough.
issues.face: Pigs with their snouts in a feed trough, wind turbines on the skyline
issues.caption: Snouts in the trough.

proofs.text: VicGrid: if Iberdrola meets expectations, it will be appointed to build, own and operate VNI West.
AusNet, owner of most of Victoria's transmission network, sold to a Canadian Brookfield led consortium.
Brookfield fund report: the Western Renewables Link is a "~A$4 billion" project, with "potential returns".

issues.title: Labor downright ignored farmers
issues.punch: More than 10,000 emails to the Premier. His answer? Fines.
issues.body: Farmers and the Victorians who back them have sent more than 10,000 emails to Premier Ben Carroll's office. As one of his first acts as Premier, twelve farmers opposing VNI West were hit with $814 fines for refusing VicGrid access to their own land. Dingwall farmers Mary and Colin Fenton, in their eighties, were among them.
issues.teaser: More than 10,000 emails to the Premier. Twelve farmers fined $814 anyway.
issues.face: A padlocked farm gate with a notice tied to it and a survey flag in the paddock
issues.caption: Ignored, then fined at their own gate.

proofs.text: Ben Carroll became Victoria's Premier on 28 July 2026.
Twelve farmers opposing VNI West fined $814 for refusing VicGrid access.
Twelve landholders, including Mary and Colin Fenton, refuse to pay the $814 fines.
More than 10,000 emails sent to the Premier's office.

groups.label: Devastating cities
groups.sub: Debt, broken promises and a fragile food supply

issues.title: Labor has bankrupted Victoria and you will pay
issues.punch: $175 billion in debt. About $24 million a day in interest.
issues.body: Labor's own budget has net debt hitting $175.6 billion this financial year and $199.3 billion by 2030, with interest of $8.9 billion this year rising to more than $32 million a day. The West Gate Tunnel blew out from $5.5 billion to $10.2 billion. Victoria has been downgraded by S&P and Moody's, and Labor replaced the fire services levy with a bigger emergency services levy on every property.
issues.teaser: Net debt heading to $199 billion. Interest over $32 million a day.
issues.face: Unpaid bills, a calculator and an empty wallet on a kitchen table
issues.caption: Billions in debt, and you pay the interest.

proofs.text: 2026/27 Budget: net debt $175.6b (2026/27) rising to $199.3b (2029/30); interest $8.9b rising to $11.8b, over $32m a day.
West Gate Tunnel: initially $5.5 billion, blown out to $10.2 billion.
S&P cut Victoria from AAA to AA; Moody's stripped the AAA, then cut again to Aa2.
PBO: Suburban Rail Loop East and North put at $200.3 billion to build and operate.

issues.title: Labor lied about its renewables policies
issues.punch: $1.5 billion to you. $4 billion to the owner's investors.
issues.body: Labor kept quoting $1.53 billion for the Western Renewables Link, while the owner's Canadian parent told its investors about $4 billion. On 15 September the Premier ordered a cost review that reports after the election, then the planning approval was gazetted on 30 September anyway. Labor promised the SEC would keep bills down, yet electricity prices rose 13.2% in the year to August.
issues.teaser: $1.5 billion here. About $4 billion to the owner's investors. Approved anyway.
issues.face: Giant transmission towers right behind a row of suburban houses
issues.caption: The renewables promise, broken.

proofs.text: Premier orders a Western Renewables Link cost review on 15 September, reporting by the end of 2026; PwC put the cost at $1.53b.
Brookfield fund annual report: the line is a "~A$4 billion" project.
Western Renewables Link planning approval gazetted 30 September 2026.
ABS: electricity prices up 13.2% in the year to August 2026.

issues.title: Labor has put Victoria's food supply under threat
issues.punch: Pave the paddocks, string up the towers, then wonder why shelves empty.
issues.body: Victoria is Australia's biggest food and fibre exporter, 28% of the national total. Yet the VFF estimates more than 100,000 hectares of farmland has gone to housing in ten years, while Labor declares renewable energy zones and runs transmission over prime country. When panic buying hit in March, shelves emptied fast: our food chain is fragile, and Labor keeps chipping away at the farms that feed it.
issues.teaser: Australia's biggest food exporter, losing farmland to housing estates and power lines.
issues.face: A supermarket aisle of empty shelves and an abandoned trolley
issues.caption: A fragile food chain, and fewer farms to feed it.

proofs.text: Victoria: Australia's largest food and fibre exporter, $22.1 billion, 28% of the national total.
VFF: more than 100,000 hectares of farmland lost to housing in the past 10 years.
Five renewable energy zones declared, plus an offshore zone.
March 2026: panic buying emptied fuel bowsers and supermarket shelves.
